concept.technique_name: contrast and echo signal words in text completion

examples.problem_statement: Though some judges have found in the Third Amendment to the US Constitution a (i) _________ for a right to privacy, it was drafted primarily to appease opponents of the Constitution, and was particularly a (ii) _________ to those antifederalists who sought to prevent the new state from maintaining a standing army. Since Article 1, section 8 of the Constitution explicitly grants to Congress the power to raise and maintain an army, the Third Amendment was largely (iii) _________ before it was written.

solution.operation: Register the opening signal word "though" and set the first clause in opposition to the second clause
solution.result: The clause holding blank (i) must oppose the statement that the Amendment was actually meant to appease opponents
solution.description: Read the sentence's pivot word first: "though" forces the judges' privacy reading to stand against the Amendment's real appeasement purpose, which is what fixes the direction of blank (i).

solution.operation: Select the blank (i) word that names something judges could find in the Amendment as support for a privacy right
solution.description: Apply the opposition you just established: the word must make the judges' reading a genuine grounding for privacy, and "basis" is the best choice among the options.

solution.operation: Echo the word "appease" from the same sentence into blank (ii)
solution.result: sop, which can mean "something given to pacify"
solution.description: The second blank is not a contrast but a restatement, so copy the sentence's own word "appease" and pick the option closest in meaning to it.

solution.operation: Use the fact that Article 1, section 8 already granted Congress army powers to fix blank (iii)
solution.description: Since the cited Article makes the Third Amendment a matter of only abstract concern, the blank needs a word meaning "of no practical importance," and "moot" delivers exactly that.

key_reminders: "Though" at the head of a sentence signals that the clause containing the blank opposes what follows.
A blank can echo a nearby word rather than contrast with it -- look for the word the sentence hands you (here, "appease").
A supporting fact cited later in the passage can define a blank's meaning outright.
common_mistakes: Treating blank (ii) as another contrast and reversing it, when the sentence asks it to echo "appease."
Filling blank (i) with a negative word such as "detriment" or "counterargument" by attaching the contrast to the wrong half of the "though" construction.

examples.problem_statement: Select one entry for the blank from the corresponding column of choices, filling the blank in the way that best completes the text. The children's ______ natures were in sharp contrast to the even-tempered dispositions of their parents.

solution.operation: Read "in sharp contrast to" as instructing that the children's natures oppose the parents' natures
solution.result: The blank must mean the opposite of "even-tempered"
solution.description: Identify the sentence's contrast marker and use it to set the required meaning of the blank against the described parents.

solution.operation: Match "the opposite of even-tempered" to a choice meaning quickly changing
solution.description: Test the choices against the meaning you derived; "mercurial," meaning quickly changing, fits that requirement exactly.

solution.operation: Check blithe (happy), phlegmatic (unemotional), apathetic (uncaring), and cunning for any sense of changing from one state to another
solution.result: None of them suggests a tendency to change, so none contrasts with "even-tempered" as well
solution.description: Eliminate the remaining temperament words by confirming they describe a temperament without describing instability, which is the specific quality the contrast demands.

key_reminders: "In sharp contrast to" requires the blank to mean the opposite of the trait it is contrasted with.
"Even-tempered" opposes not any temperament, but specifically a changeable one.
common_mistakes: Choosing any word that merely names a temperament (blithe, phlegmatic, apathetic) instead of one that specifically means changeable.

concept.technique_name: testing cases against a median definition
concept.sub_category: median of a data set / quantitative comparison

examples.problem_statement: Compare Quantity A and Quantity B, using the additional information given. In a set of 24 positive integers, 12 of the integers are less than 50. The rest are greater than 50. Quantity A: the median of the 24 integers. Quantity B: 50.

solution.operation: State the median rule for a set of n integers with n even: order them least to greatest and average the two middle integers
solution.description: Begin from the definition of the median for an even-sized set, since that is what determines Quantity A.

solution.operation: Apply the given split of the 24 integers to identify what is known about the two middle values
solution.result: 12 integers are below 50 and 12 above 50, so a_{12} < 50 < a_{13}, but neither value itself is known
solution.description: Translate the condition on the set into a statement about the two middle positions, which is the only place the median comes from.

solution.result: \frac{49 + 51}{2} = 50, so Quantity A equals Quantity B
solution.description: Test a first admissible case to see one possible relationship between the median and 50.

solution.result: \frac{49 + 53}{2} = 51, so Quantity A exceeds Quantity B
solution.description: Test a second admissible case that still respects the split, producing a different relationship from the first case.

solution.operation: Compare the two cases, which give different relationships under the same given information
solution.description: Conclude from the conflicting cases that no single relationship follows from the information given, which selects the "cannot be determined" choice.

examples.answer: Choice D: The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.

key_reminders: For an even number of values, the median is the average of the two middle values after ordering.
Knowing only how many values fall on each side of a number does not pin down the middle values themselves.
Two admissible cases giving different relationships is sufficient to answer "cannot be determined."
common_mistakes: Assuming the 12-below / 12-above split forces the median to equal 50.
Stopping after the single case 49 and 51 and answering "the two quantities are equal."

concept.technique_name: sign rules for products and odd exponents

examples.problem_statement: If B^3 A < 0 and A > 0, which of the following must be negative? (A) AB (B) B^2 A (C) B^4

solution.operation: Recognize that the inequality has 0 on one side, so the question is testing rules of positives and negatives
solution.result: Treat B^3 A < 0 as a statement about signs rather than magnitudes
solution.description: Notice the zero on one side of the inequality, which is the cue to reason about signs instead of trying to solve for values.

solution.operation: Given A > 0 and B^3 A < 0, deduce the sign of B^3
solution.description: Since a positive factor cannot make a product negative on its own, the other factor must carry the negative sign.

solution.operation: Apply the rule that a number raised to an odd exponent retains the sign of its base
solution.description: Move from the sign of B^3 back to the sign of B itself, which is valid because the exponent 3 is odd.

solution.operation: Multiply the positive A by the negative B
solution.description: Combine the two established signs: a positive times a negative is negative, so AB must be negative.

key_reminders: A product is negative only if exactly one of its factors is negative.
A number raised to an odd exponent keeps the sign of its base.
An inequality compared with 0 is a sign question, not a magnitude question.
common_mistakes: Concluding B^2 A or B^4 is negative, when an even exponent makes B^2 and B^4 nonnegative regardless of B's sign.
Failing to carry the sign of B^3 back to B because the odd-exponent rule was overlooked.
